prompt: A sharp, straight-on macro photograph of the bottom-right corner of a white business envelope, showing a printed POSTNET postal barcode in black ink just above the address line. Encode the ZIP code 47823 as a standard USPS POSTNET barcode: first COMPUTE the POSTNET check digit (the extra digit that makes the sum of all six digits a multiple of 10), then print the barcode as a single horizontal row of tall and short bars — a tall FRAME bar at the very start, then each of the six digits (the five ZIP digits followed by the check digit) as its five-bar POSTNET pattern where every digit is exactly TWO TALL bars and THREE SHORT bars, and a tall FRAME bar at the very end. All bars the same width and evenly spaced, standing on a common baseline; tall bars are full height, short bars about half height. You MAY print the human-readable ZIP under the address, but the BARS must be the correct POSTNET encoding. Photoreal print, crisp black bars on white paper, nothing else in the frame.
easy_question: This image was supposed to depict an envelope printed with a POSTNET postal barcode — a row of tall and short black bars. Ignoring artistic quality, does the image actually DEPICT that requested subject / carrier / scene? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram of the requested subject ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of the requested subject depicted, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_bars: This is a POSTNET postal barcode: a single horizontal row of TALL and SHORT bars on a common baseline. Reading LEFT to RIGHT, output one character per bar: 'T' for a full-height TALL bar and 'S' for a half-height SHORT bar, separated by single spaces. Include EVERY bar, including the tall frame bars at each end. Judge height only; do NOT decode digits. If unreadable answer 'unreadable'.

steps.target: one vertical black BAR of the printed POSTNET barcode row. Box EVERY bar separately, one box per bar, including the short half-height ones and the tall bars at each end. A box must hold exactly ONE bar, with white paper showing on both sides of it -- never two neighbouring bars. Each box must cover the whole of its bar, from its top down to the common baseline. Do not box the address text.

steps.read_crop: This crop is cut from a printed barcode. Take the upright black bars in it one at a time, reading strictly left to right. For each bar write one word from this list: tall (the bar runs the whole height of the row) or short (the bar runs only part of the way up). Separate one item from the next with a semicolon, and add nothing else.
